items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear, but restoreQueries in createPersister.ts now holds a long inline merge (status/error/data comparisons ending in existingQuery.setState({...})) with no comments. The queryObserver change (`...(query.state.data !== undefined && state.fetchFailureCount > 0 && {...})`) is not explained.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: persisterFn and bulk restoreQueries don't share a restore/merge helper. Bulk merges inline and applies it with existingQuery.setState, so the logic is duplicated. Core uses setState instead of a dedicated reducer action. The queryObserver hack special-cases failure counts. Public types use PersisterRestoreResult<T, any>.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Persisted state is not normalised. createPersisterRestoreResult passes `state: result.state` through unchanged, with no checks on counts or timestamps and no status/error consistency check. isPersisterRestoreResult uses `(value as any)._persisterRestoreResult`. The core restore path does force fetchStatus to 'idle'.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: The helper is exported and Query checks for the marker, returning before the success path so no callbacks fire. But the marker has a forgeable duck-typed fallback (`'_persisterRestoreResult' in value`). Bulk restore duplicates the merge instead of sharing one apply path, and there is no dedicated restore action.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: Persisters that return plain data still take the normal setData path, the new exports are additive, and the createPersister options are unchanged. However, queryObserver now skips fetchState during 'isRestoring' and carries fetchFailureCount into optimistic results, an internal behaviour shift that existing tests don't cover.
